title: Design YouTube / Netflix Video Streaming
subtitle: Pre-signed S3 upload, DAG chunk transcoding, HLS/ABR & Edge CDN
functionalReqs: Creators upload multi-GB raw 4K videos reliably with pause/resume.
Transcode videos asynchronously into multi-bitrate HLS/DASH segments (360p, 720p, 1080p, 4K).
Viewers stream smoothly via Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) switching based on live bandwidth.
Serve popular catalog videos at sub-50ms Time-to-First-Frame globally via CDN.

nonFunctionalReqs.rationale: Multi-GB uploads over unstable Wi-Fi must never route through API pods or restart from 0%.
Buffering stalls cause immediate viewer drop-off.

nonFunctionalReqs.target: Tbps global egress offloaded to CDN
nonFunctionalReqs.rationale: Origin servers cannot handle millions of concurrent video streams directly.

workedSummary.uploadVolume: 500k new videos/day (~50 TB raw/day -> ~100 TB/day across ABR encodings)
workedSummary.cdnOffload: 95%+ of segment fetches served directly from Edge/ISP Open-Connect CDN PoPs

apiContracts.purpose: Mint VideoMetadata record and return chunked Pre-Signed S3 Multipart Upload URLs
Return HLS Adaptive Bitrate manifest listing available resolution playlists

explorerTopology.title: Chunked Upload, Parallel DAG Transcoding & Edge ABR Streaming
explorerTopology.subtitle: Pre-signed S3 multipart -> GOP split workers -> HLS manifest -> Edge CDN PoP
explorerTopology.overview: Proxying a 4 GB creator upload through app servers exhausts pod RAM and bandwidth, while encoding a 2-hour movie on one CPU takes hours. Pre-signed S3 multipart uploads bypass API servers completely, a DAG splits the video by Group-of-Pictures (GOP) chunks across 50 parallel encoding workers, and Edge CDNs deliver 4-second HLS/DASH segments globally.
keyTakeaways: Upload chunks directly from browser/mobile to S3 via Pre-Signed URLs—API pods handle only metadata.
Parallelize transcoding by splitting raw video at GOP keyframes into 4s chunks encoded concurrently across a DAG.
Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) clients dynamically switch between 360p/720p/1080p per 4-second segment as network throughput fluctuates.

nodes.label: Creator / Viewer App
nodes.summary: Uploads 8 MB parts directly to S3 or streams 4s HLS chunks from closest CDN.
failureModes: Monolithic MP4 playback stalls completely on mobile bandwidth drops

nodes.label: Global Edge CDN / ISP PoP
nodes.summary: Absorbs 95%+ of Tbps global video playback traffic right inside local ISP/Edge PoPs.
failureModes: Cold long-tail videos miss cache and fall back via Origin Shield

nodes.label: S3 Raw + Encoded Store
nodes.summary: Receives resumable multipart uploads directly without tying up app servers; stores final `.m4s` segments.
failureModes: Routing uploads through app servers creates immediate OOM/NIC bottlenecks

nodes.label: Parallel DAG Transcoders
nodes.summary: Triggered by S3 completion event; splits video into 4s GOP chunks and encodes all bitrates in parallel.
whenToUse: Cutting 2-hour transcode time down to minutes
failureModes: Unbounded queue backlog—prioritize lower resolutions (360p/720p) first so playback goes live fast

nodes.label: Video Metadata DB
nodes.summary: Tracks upload state, DRM keys, and publishes video live once 360p/720p/1080p manifests finish.
failureModes: Coupling large binary reads with metadata SQL queries

steps.info: Creator uploads 256 × 8MB parts straight to S3 using pre-signed URLs (0 proxy load!)
steps.inspectorNote: Chunking allows automatic resume of just Part #14 on Wi-Fi hiccups without restarting a 2 GB file.

steps.info: Video split into 4s GOP chunks -> encoded across 48 parallel workers -> 360p/720p/1080p
steps.inspectorNote: Publishing 360p/720p immediately makes the video playable within seconds while 4K finishes asynchronously.

steps.info: Viewer fetches master.m3u8 -> 1080p/seg_01.m4s served from Edge PoP in 12ms
steps.payloadInspector: Player measures throughput=18Mbps -> selects 1080p variant seamlessly
steps.inspectorNote: Notice how each 4s segment is immutable and content-addressed, giving >95% global CDN hit ratio.

chaosScenarios.title: Viewer Bandwidth Plummets Mid-Stream -> Seamless ABR Downshift
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Mobile viewer enters an elevator; measured bandwidth drops from 25 Mbps to 1.2 Mbps.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: HLS player checks buffer + last segment download speed and immediately requests the next 4s segment (`seg_02.m4s`) from the `480p` playlist—zero rebuffer stall.

steps.info: Throughput dropped -> player fetches 480p/seg_02.m4s (140 KB instead of 1.8 MB)
steps.payloadInspector: ABR Controller: bw=1.2Mbps -> Downshift 1080p -> 480p on seg_02 boundary
steps.inspectorNote: Because all resolution variants share identical 4-second GOP segment boundaries, switching quality mid-playback is frame-accurate.

pros: Top 5% viral titles pushed to ISP PoPs overnight (zero backbone cost)
Long-tail titles cached lazily on Pull CDN
cons: Needs popularity predictor + edge storage management
Hours-long Creator wait time before video goes live

deepDives.title: Per-Title Encoding Optimization
deepDives.bottleneck: Using fixed bitrate ladders wastes 4K bitrate on simple cartoons while starving fast-action sports.
deepDives.solution: Run lightweight scene-complexity analysis inside the DAG to compute a custom bitrate-resolution ladder per title (Netflix approach), cutting bandwidth 20–40% at equal VMAF quality.
deepDives.tradeoff: Slightly higher upfront transcode CPU cost saved thousands of times over in CDN egress.

deepDives.title: Handling Viral Long-Tail Cache Misses
deepDives.bottleneck: A sudden tweet sends 50k viewers to an obscure 5-year-old video absent from Edge PoPs.
deepDives.solution: Shield S3 Origin behind a regional Origin Shield tier with request coalescing so Edge PoPs never stampede S3.
deepDives.tradeoff: First cold viewers see +15ms shield hop before edge caches warm.

criteria: Uses Pre-Signed S3 Multipart directly from client
Estimates PB storage & Tbps CDN offload
Splits video by GOP keyframes into parallel chunks
Publishes lower bitrates first for fast live time
Uses Origin Shield + Push/Pull hybrid CDN
Separates metadata SQL from blob S3 reads
